title: Number of Islands
description:
The grid `grid` contains `"1"` for land and `"0"` for water. An **island** is a maximal set of land cells linked through horizontal or vertical neighbours (diagonals do not count). Everything outside the grid is water.

Return how many islands there are.
hints: Each island is one connected component of land cells. How could you count components?
Scan the grid; whenever you meet land you have not visited, you have found a new island.
From that cell flood-fill all connected land (mark it visited or sink it to '0'), then continue scanning. Prefer an explicit stack/queue: a 300x300 island is too deep for plain recursion.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def numIslands(self, grid: List[List[str]]) -> int:

args.$py: [["1" if (i+j)%2==0 else "0" for j in range(300)] for i in range(300)]
[["1" if (i%2==0 or (i%4==1 and j==299) or (i%4==3 and j==0)) else "0" for j in range(300)] for i in range(299)]

solution.explanation: Scan every cell. On unvisited land, add one to the answer and flood-fill the whole island with an explicit stack, setting visited land to '0' so it is never counted again. Each cell is pushed at most once, so time is O(m*n); the stack can hold O(m*n) cells in the worst case. Using a stack instead of recursion avoids hitting the recursion limit on large islands.
